detail.title: LEY 21.521, LA PRESTACIÓN DE SERVICIOS FINANCIEROS FINTECH: EL DESAFIO DE LA COMISIÓN PARA EL MERCADO FINANCIERO PARA REGULARLOS (Act N°21.521/2023, The Provision Of Financial Services In Fintech: The Challenge For The Financial Market Comission To Regulate Them)
detail.abstract:
Spanish Abstract: El presente trabajo tiene la finalidad de describir y evaluar, dentro de la ley N° 21.521, cuales son las empresas Fintech afectadas a esta norma legal, como se ven afectadas por la nueva regulación, cuales son los parámetros mínimos que deben cumplir, etc. De igual forma, es importante tener en cuenta las facultades de regulación otorgadas a la CMF; sus responsabilidades como entidad fiscalizadora de las empresas tecnológicas emergentes Fintech es suficiente o debe ser complementada por actos administrativos y la doctrina nacional como internacional.

Se buscará aclarar que sucederá con la seguridad hacía las Fintech y las personas, explicar el porque de las altas exigencias a las empresas Fintech sabiendo que existen distintas variables como, mantener la responsabilidad del empresario de responder y ser sancionado, que se permita la creación de futuros emprendimientos al igual que dar espacio a la responsabilidad conjunta existente del sistema financiero; ya que, no es sustentable un sistema de préstamos sin la existencia de seguros de las instituciones, con la finalidad de dar seguridad económica tanto a la institución como a las personas que ocupan los servicios prestados por las mismas.

Cabe destacar la posible discusión de cuál es la mejor forma en que debe actuar la CMF, frente a dicha problemática nos centraremos en su futuro actuar -de acuerdo con lo establecido en la ley del plazo de 18 meses desde promulgada y posteriormente- para mantener un equilibrio entre la economía de mercado y el respeto por las normas jurídicas vigentes. Sin olvidar el derecho comparado que por medio de la historia de la ley se demuestra su importancia para crearse la ley N° 21.521/2023.

English Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to describe and assess, within Act 21.521/2023, which Fintech companies are subject to this legal provision, how they are affected by the new regulation, what mínimum parameters they must meet, and so on. Likewise, it is important to take into account the regulatory powers granted to the FMC, its responsibilities as a supervisory entity for emerging Fintech technology companies, the scope of activity of these companies, whether the legal description of Fintech companies is sufficient or should by supplemented by administrative acts and both national and international doctrine.

The aim is to clarify what will happen with the security of Fintech companies and individuals, explain the reason behind the high demands placed on Fintech companies given the existence of different variables, such as maintaining the entrepreneur's responsibility to respond and be sanctioned, allowing the creation of future ventures, as well as providing space for the shared responsibility that exists within the financial system. This is because a lending system without institutional insurance is unsustainable, as such insurance is essential to provide economic security both to the institution and to the people who use its services.

It is worth highlighting the potencial debate on the best way for the FMC to act in this matter. Faced with this issue, we will focus on its future actions -according to the provisions in the law, which establishes a period of 18 months from its enactment and thereafter- to maintain a balance between the market economy and respect for the existing legal framework. This is without overlooking comparative law, which, through the legislative history, demonstrates its importance in the creation of Act 21.521/2023.

detail.abstract: Large-scale movement of animals through trade can spread diseases to places where theyare not endemic. We identify the causal e ect of global livestock trade on the spread ofinfectious animal diseases through an exogenous increase in demand for imported livestock.The instrumental variable approach exploits an increase in halal livestock importsin Muslim countries during the major religious festival of Eid al-Adha. Using monthlydata for 123 countries, ve livestock categories, and sixteen years, we nd an imports-toinfectionselasticity of about 0.75. The relationship is stronger for countries that are likelyto import infected livestock from their partners, or that are endowed with large domesticlivestock. These results highlight transmission through trade from origin to destination.

title: Digital Transformation and Global Trade: Opportunities and Challenges for Emerging Economies
affiliations: University of Hertfordshire

detail.title: Digital Transformation and Global Trade: Opportunities and Challenges for Emerging Economies
detail.abstract: Digital globalization has transformed the landscape of international business, reshaping trade flows, investment patterns, and cross-border collaboration. For emerging economies like India, the acceleration of digital technologies presents both opportunities and challenges. This article critically examines the implications of digital globalization for India in the coming decade. Drawing on recent reports from the World Bank, UNCTAD, and leading scholars, the paper highlights key opportunities in e-commerce expansion, digital services exports, innovation ecosystems, and global value chains. At the same time, it considers the challenges of digital inequality, cybersecurity threats, regulatory gaps, and geopolitical uncertainties. The discussion emphasizes how India can position itself strategically by investing in digital infrastructure, upskilling human capital, fostering entrepreneurship, and strengthening policy frameworks. Ultimately, the article argues that India stands at a pivotal moment: by leveraging digital globalization effectively, it can enhance its role as a major player in international business and drive inclusive economic growth.

title: When Roll-up Breaks: Serial Private Equity Acquisitions in the Hospital Industry
affiliations: Duke University - Finance

detail.title: When Roll-up Breaks: Serial Private Equity Acquisitions in the Hospital Industry
detail.abstract: This paper challenges the idea that private equity (PE) roll-ups consistently create site-level operating value across sequential acquisitions. I link hospital operations, finances, quality, and deal data and classify targets as stand-alone, platform, or add-on. Platforms are selected from low-leverage, higher-margin hospitals, consistent with grandstanding at entry. They obtain cheaper debt at close, rebalance balance sheets and investment, and then exhibit gradual profitability gains. Add-ons inherit the platform facility, cut headcount, and do not generate additional margin improvement. The evidence points to a two-stage strategy, with value created at platform formation and little scalability to add-on acquisitions in the hospital industry.

title: Project Valuation under Dual-Source Risk in Incomplete Markets: An Axiomatic Framework
affiliations: School of Business, Southern University of Science and Technology, China, Colorado State University, Fort Collins - Department of Finance & Real Estate and University of Texas at Austin

detail.title: Project Valuation under Dual-Source Risk in Incomplete Markets: An Axiomatic Framework
detail.abstract: This paper develops a unified axiomatic framework for valuing risky projects in incomplete markets where uncertainty arises from both market-traded and privately held sources. By integrating decision analysis and finance valuation approaches, we theoretically examine how the sequencing of market and private uncertainty resolutions affects valuation outcomes. Challenging the commonly held assumption of valuation order independence justified by independence or Bayesian updating in standard decision analysis, our analysis reveals that reversing the order of uncertainty resolution can materially alter valuations involving intertwined market and private risks under market incompleteness. To identify normatively robust valuation models, we propose a set of axioms and theories that formalize rational preference conditions across diverse informational structures. We further extend the framework to dynamic settings, demonstrating its consistency with mean-variance preferences and its applicability to multiperiod portfolio management. The resulting framework offers both a rigorous theoretical foundation and actionable guidance for practitioners evaluating complex investment decisions.

title: Executing trades in style: Retail investors vs. institutions
affiliations: Chulalongkorn University - Department of Banking & Finance, Chulalongkorn University - Chulalongkorn Business School and University of Luxembourg

detail.title: Executing trades in style: Retail investors vs. institutions
detail.abstract: Employing an exhaustive sample of trades made by all investors in a fully automated order-driven stock market, we examine trade execution prices between retail and institutional investors. Retail investors execute both purchases and sales systematically at better prices than domestic institutions, but receive better prices than foreign institutions only when executing sales. Importantly, we also find some evidence consistent with the hypothesis that retail investors have a comparative advantage in executing trades of small-cap stocks. Based on a population of retail trades, our findings are not consistent with the stereotype arising from earlier studies that retail investors are noise traders.

title: Intraday Proprietary Traders and Short-term Mispricing*
affiliations: Indian School of Business, Indian School of Business, Indian School of Business and Indian School of Business

detail.title: Intraday Proprietary Traders and Short-term Mispricing*
detail.abstract: Whose trading corrects temporary mispricing? We document that intraday proprietary traders play this crucial role. Using trader-level transaction data, we examine the activities of different types of traders around a media-driven, clean shock to retail trading. Intraday proprietary traders are contrarian and contribute to an immediate and sustained price correction. Their trades generate returns from informed trading rather than liquidity provision. Conversely, longer-term proprietary traders who engage in much less contrarian trading make small returns from liquidity provision, not informed trading. Thus, policies designed to curb short-termism must account for the contributions of different types of traders to price discovery.

detail.title: Wavelet Analysis and the Financial Performance of ESG-Strategies

publicationDetails.detailsText: Accepted for Handbook of ESG Investing

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information and financial performance in Europe using wavelet-based multiresolution analysis. By combining an event study approach with the Maximal Overlap Discrete Wavelet Transform (MODWT), the analysis isolates reactions to ESG-related signals and captures the temporal structure of abnormal returns. ESG signals are derived from price movements of STOXX Global ESG Leaders indices, and portfolios are constructed based on top and bottom LSEG Refinitiv ESG ratings. The results indicate that ESG effects are not short-lived but develop over medium-to long-term horizons. Environmental and social signals are gradually incorporated into asset prices under stable market conditions, while governance-related effects are more volatile and pronounced in poorly rated firms. The study contributes a novel methodological perspective by linking signal-driven performance responses with the time-frequency characteristics of returns, offering insights into the persistence of ESG information and the timing relevance of its market impact.

title: The importance of targets and value creation in vertical acquisitions
affiliations: Chulalongkorn University - Department of Banking & Finance and University of Strathclyde

detail.title: The importance of targets and value creation in vertical acquisitions
detail.abstract: We study how value creation in vertical acquisitions varies in the importance of the target’s assets to its acquirer. The synergistic gain increases in the degree of vertical relatedness between the acquirer and target industries. This finding suggests that the importance of the target firm’s assets to its acquirer’s productivity is an important value-creating channel in vertical acquisitions. We also find evidence suggesting that acquirers extract greater value as the synergistic gain increases, consistent with an efficient investment incentive underlying the integration decision.

title: Generalized Bayesian subset simulation for the evaluation of failure probability
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Generalized Bayesian subset simulation for the evaluation of failure probability
detail.abstract: Evaluation of failure probability is essential in system design and analysis. But it has become increasing prohibitive due to growing system complexity and soaring simulation costs. To address such challenge, we propose a novel active learning framework, the generalized Bayesian subset simulation (GBSS), to estimate failure probability. Based on the concept of generalized subset simulation, GBSS introduces a novel threshold-first criteria and decomposes the target failure events into an optimal sequence of intermediate events. Combined with a Bayesian surrogate model, high-quality conditional samples may be generated efficiently with residual resampling in Markov chain Monte Carlo and in turn improves model accuracy. We evaluate our framework via a comprehensive set of academic examples and industrial cases of high dimensions. Comparing to four state-of-the-art methods, including Monte Carlo, subset simulation, generalized subset simulation and multi-fidelity subset simulations, GBSS demonstrates substantial improvements in both numerical efficiency and stability.

title: Trump strikes again! Will geopolitical fragmentation be different?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National Bank of Poland and National Bank of Poland

detail.title: Trump strikes again! Will geopolitical fragmentation be different?
detail.abstract: We examine trade effects of US tariff increases introduced by Donald Trump by May 2025, using a New Quantitative Trade model calibrated to 45 countries and 56 industries. In addition to scenarios based on official announcements, we analyze one scenario that incorporates actual changes in effective US tariff rates for detailed product categories. We separate the roles of tariff hikes, exemptions, and retaliation in driving changes in key macroeconomic variables. Our findings indicate that the tariff shock acts as like a negative supply shock for the US, and as a demand shock for its major partners. Tariff-driven trade adjustments reinforce geoeconomic fragmentation, particularly within the Western bloc.

title: Handing Over the Keys to the City: When Governments May Inadvertently Solve One Crisis with a Bigger One
affiliations: University of Cambridge, University of Cambridge, University of Cologne and Cornell University - College of Arts & Sciences

detail.title: Handing Over the Keys to the City: When Governments May Inadvertently Solve One Crisis with a Bigger One

keywords: Handing Over the Keys to the City

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of "handing over the keys to the city", whereby political leaders facing severe crises delegate (potentially excessive) decision-making authority and/or operational control to external entities perceived as holding indispensable solutions. While intended to resolve the initial crisis, this delegation has the potential to inadvertently create larger, more intractable problems, and the desperation felt during a crisis can push leaders into Faustian pacts, trading control for perceived salvation. We develop a conceptual framework to analyse situations where governments hand over the keys to the city, presenting typologies for different crises, the types of key that can be delegated, and the extent to which such delegation(s) can occur. We conclude by drawing out the policy implications, and outlining a research agenda.

title: A Data-Driven Stochastic Multi-Objective Framework for Sustainable Oil-Palm Seed Distribution: Scenario, Sensitivity, and Robustness Analytics
affiliations: Universitas Sumatera Utara, Universitas Medan Area and Universitas Medan Area

detail.title: A Data-Driven Stochastic Multi-Objective Framework for Sustainable Oil-Palm Seed Distribution: Scenario, Sensitivity, and Robustness Analytics
detail.abstract: ABTRACTThe distribution of oil palm seedlings (KKS) plays a strategic role in the sustainability of the plantation system but is faced with budget constraints, variations in distribution costs, and inter-regional disparities. This study develops a data driven multiobjective stochastic optimization framework to balance three main dimensions involve coverage, equity, and cost efficiency. Utilizing historical KKS distribution data and designing baseline, high-cost, and low-budget scenarios, this study formulates three approaches: a deterministic model as the baseline, a two-stage risk-neutral (RN) stochastic optimization, and a riskaverse (RA) expansion using Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR). The results indicate that the RN model is able to increase national coverage by 0.72 but results in higher inequality by 0.11. Conversely, the RA model reduces inequality by 0.09 with a relatively small decrease in coverage by 0.70 and better cost control. Sensitivity analysis confirms that indicator weights and policy targets strongly influence coverage, while risk penalties have a greater influence on inequality. Under extreme scenarios of cost increases, budget cuts, and decreased efficiency, robustness tests demonstrate that RA is more stable, equitable, and efficient than RN. Beyond KKS distribution, this approach can be applied to other resource allocation systems to support equitable, efficient, and resilient plantation policies.

title: From Chornobyl to War: The Cost of Corruption to Ukraine’s Environment
affiliations: Dublin City University and Dublin City University Business School

detail.title: From Chornobyl to War: The Cost of Corruption to Ukraine’s Environment

Each participant was provided with a Participant Information Sheet. The Informed Consent Form was complited by each participant prior to the interview.

detail.abstract: In this chapter, we analyse the impact of corruption on the environment in Ukraine. Ukraine is an ideal case study for the effects of corruption on the environment having been part of the Soviet Union and suffering a catastrophic environmental disaster in part due to the systematic corruption of that state. Post-independence Ukraine continues to struggle with corruption, despite some significant progress. Moreover, the full-scale Russian invasion of 2022, launched by a kleptocratic regime and implemented by a corrupt military, has devasted Ukraine's environment and poses an ongoing threat to the global environment. We analyse data from interviews conducted in 2024 and 2025 with members of Ukrainian civil society involved in environmental activism, experts in environmental law and environmental protection, and with experience in the community and state sector relating to the environment. Based on the analysis of these data, we describe Ukrainians' assessment of the impact of corruption on the environment, the dynamics of the fight against corruption in the 21 st century and the factors that have influenced it. We highlight the most common manifestations of corruption that our respondents have encountered, as well as their assessment of the impact of the war on the spread of corruption. We summarise respondents' opinions on effective ways to combat corruption in the environmental sector. The chapter therefore provides insights into corruption patterns and potential anti-corruption strategies to protect the environment.

title: Embryonic Option-hood
affiliations: Arizona State University (ASU) - Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law, Vanderbilt University - Law School and Vanderbilt University - Law School

detail.title: Embryonic Option-hood

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

publicationDetails.journalName: Arizona State University Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: A frozen embryo does not merely represent a potential for human life; it represents a deferred decision to trigger this potential. Parties value this decision deferral because it allows them to retain the option to attempt conception after any uncertainty about future events or desires has resolved. Failing to recognize this “option value” of embryos has resulted in confusion over the best approach to allocating ownership of embryos and calculating damages for reproductive harms. This Article provides a novel paradigm showing that embryos should be treated as neither persons nor mere property; instead, a significant portion of their value is in their ability to preserve and defer decisions over implantation. When such embryonic option-hood is overlooked, society risks improperly allocating disposition rights and undercompensating patients who were deprived of this option. Given this insight, this Article makes two significant contributions. First, this Article proposes a modified approach to embryo disposition that validates—rather than undermines—the option value of embryos. In the absence of a valid contract, most courts balance party interests at the time of conflict. Because this approach is not focused on party expectations at the time of embryo creation, reliance on the traditional balancing test can essentially destroy the option value of embryos. This Article adds an intermediate step before resorting to balancing which requires the court to make a fact-intensive determination into whether there was an agreed-upon disposition at the time of embryo creation. In the absence of evidence of original intent, the Article proposes a modified version of the traditional balancing test courts have used. Second, acknowledging the option value of embryos sheds light on how to calculate damages in different contexts. This Article establishes a methodology for determining both the standard of care/regulatory standards necessary to protect embryos as well as damages for compensating patients for negligence resulting in embryo loss and for intentional interference with embryos. The Article concludes by cautioning that state interference newly allowed by Dobbs can eviscerate the option value of embryos, with upstream effects for embryo creation and fertility care access.

title: Ethical, Legal, and Social Issues (ELSI) in the Conversion of Existing Airport Facilities to Spaceports
affiliations: Keio University, Chiba University - Chiba University Hospital, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Ethical, Legal, and Social Issues (ELSI) in the Conversion of Existing Airport Facilities to Spaceports
detail.abstract: This study conducts a systematic literature review to identify and analyze the ethical, legal, and social issues (ELSI) associated with converting airports into spaceports. Using seven academic databases, 343 records were screened, and 17 studies were selected for detailed analysis. Ten key ELSI categories were extracted, including economic impact, pollution, sonic booms, aviation disruption, safety, public health, and insurance. While many issues are broadly relevant to spaceports, some, such as cost-effectiveness and airspace management, are specific to airport-to-spaceport conversion. To contextualize the findings, Oita Airport in Japan was analyzed as a case study. Two projects were reviewed: a satellite launch project (since canceled) and an ongoing spaceplane landing plan. Oita Airport’s coastal location, low air traffic, and existing infrastructure make it suitable for spaceport use, although its lack of medical facilities remains a concern. The study concludes that airports suitable for conversion should (1) be located away from densely populated areas, (2) have low interference with existing aviation operations, and (3) possess or be connected to sufficient medical infrastructure. The analysis underscores the need for a cost-benefit approach when evaluating public investments in such projects, especially considering potential disruptions to aviation and the need for public accountability. The paper highlights gaps in the current literature, such as the absence of empirical data and lack of regulatory clarity, and recommends future research focused on stakeholder engagement, implementation feedback, and the development of standardized ELSI frameworks for emerging spaceports.

Italian abstract: Le conseguenze sulle economie locali di crisi industriali e chiusure di stabilimenti che occupano una quota rilevante di manodopera sono state oggetto di un interesse relativamente recente da parte della letteratura. Applicando il metodo del controllo sintetico ad un evento che ha interessato un’area del Sud Italia specializzata nella produzione di autoveicoli se ne quantificano gli effetti economici di lungo periodo sul territorio interessato. La chiusura dello stabilimento FIAT di Termini Imerese ha ridotto in maniera persistente il livello e il tasso di occupazione, determinando una diminuzione della popolazione in età da lavoro, un calo del reddito disponibile e delle quotazioni immobiliari.

English abstract: The consequences for local economies of industrial crises and the closure of plants employing a large share of the workforce have only recently attracted attention in the literature. This study quantifies the long-term economic effects of an event that occurred in an area of Southern Italy specializing in motor vehicle production, by applying the synthetic control method. The closure of the FIAT plant in Termini Imerese (Sicily) has persistently lowered the employment level and rate, leading to a decline in the working-age population, disposable income and house prices.

title: Is Quad Graphics Decision Innocuous or a Jurisprudential Threat?
affiliations: University of Connecticut - School of Law

detail.title: Is Quad Graphics Decision Innocuous or a Jurisprudential Threat?
detail.abstract:
Professor Pomp criticizes the North Carolina Supreme Court decision in Quad Graphics Inc. v. N.C. Dep't of Revenue. Professor Pomp critically examines the broader implications of this decision, especially the North Carolina Supreme Court's overruling Supreme Court precedent. Specifically, the state court interpreted Complete Auto and Wayfair as overruling Dilworth, even though Dilworth had not been overruled explicitly by the Supreme Court. 

This article argues that viewing Dilworth as having been overruled also ignores decisions after Dilworth, such as National Geographic and Jefferson Lines. These cases reaffirmed Dilworth and ignored the lower court's claim that Complete Auto implicitly rejected the formalistic distinction between sales and use taxes. Professor Pomp notes that Wayfair did not cite Dilworth, which the North Carolina court nonetheless viewed as Wayfair implicitly overruling Dilworth. Professor Pomp explains how the lower court did not appreciate the litigating posture in Wayfair, which would have made a Dilworth argument an unnecessary distraction and delay.

If lower courts can overturn Supreme Court precedent on their own, chaos will result as fifty states may have inconsistent views. Quad Graphics may embolden states to test the boundaries of their taxing power in a manner that conflicts with existing Supreme Court precedent, creating uncertainty and upsetting reliance interests.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the challenges associated with the marketing and processing of locally produced rice, with a particular focus on processors in Ivo Local Government Area (LGA) of Ebonyi State, Nigeria. The specific objectives were to: examine the effects of taxes on rice marketing and processing, evaluate the impact of transportation costs on rice sales and processing, and assess the influence of technological advancements on rice marketing and processing. A survey research design was adopted, and data were collected using structured questionnaires administered to rice processors. Descriptive statistics and regression analysis, supported by the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) Version 25, were employed to analyze the data. To strengthen the strategic evaluation, SWOT and PESTEL analytical frameworks were also applied. The findings revealed that multiple levies, high transportation expenses, and limited technological innovations significantly constrain rice processing and marketing in the study area (p < 0.05). The study recommends reducing taxation through policy reforms, improving transport infrastructure to ease logistics costs, and promoting technological adoption via equipment subsidies and capacity-building initiatives. These measures are critical for enhancing the competitiveness, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness of rice processing and marketing, thereby contributing to local food security and rural economic development.

The results demonstrate a proportional relationship between rising water temperature, organic matter content, algal biomass, and the incidence of Trichodina sp. parasitism in carp larvae.

detail.title: Imams and Patrons: Service Provision by Islamist Non-State Actors
detail.abstract: Whether armed or unarmed, Islamist non-state actors have a reputation for winning over citizens' support and spreading their ideas through service delivery, reflecting a worldwide trend in non-state service provision. While existing research attributes the notable variation in service provision to strategic targeting, we argue that service allocation is also highly dependent on a non-state actor's ability to marshal resources through local economic elites. Our findings demonstrate that service provision by religious non-state actors is more likely in areas and periods where there is associational involvement among elite supporters at the local level. For our inferences, we examine the spatial and temporal variation in the service delivery of a major Islamist group in Turkey. We use original data on non-state service infrastructure, local business associations, charitable endowments, and economic development, as proxied by average nightlight density, along with data on public service infrastructure and historical state-building institutions.

detail.title: Manager Taxation and Investment Horizon
detail.abstract: We examine whether a targeted change in manager-level tax policy affects fund-level investment behavior. The 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) extended the required holding period for carried interest to qualify for long-term capital gains treatment from one to three years. Using a difference-indifferences design and hand-collected data on fund compensation structures, we find that performance funds subject to the rule significantly increased their investment horizons relative to unaffected funds. This effect is concentrated among funds with prior holding periods near the previous threshold and fund that are tax-sensitive. Our findings document a novel institutional lock-in effect, in which fund managers delay asset sales to preserve their own tax benefits-even when such delays may harm fund performance. We provide suggestive evidence of value destruction among high-performing treated funds, highlighting how narrowly targeted tax reforms can produce unintended distortions in capital allocation and investor outcomes.

detail.abstract: The National Education Policy (NEP 2020) represents a landmark reform in India’s education system, designed to reshape the nation’s academic framework. This review offers an in-depth assessment of NEP 2020, highlighting its alignment with global educational practices, focus on skill-based advancement, and potential influence on student learning achievements, teacher development, and educational infrastructure. The policy’s intellectual significance lies in its capacity to foster inclusivity, excellence, and innovation within Indian education, tackling persistent challenges while equipping learners for the demands of the 21st century. The policy represents a pivotal step towards modernizing education and aligning it with global standards. However, its success will depend on effective implementation, stakeholder engagement, and ongoing research.

detail.title: Moral Philosophy and Archetypes in the Symbolic Cohesion of the Legend of the Tunjo
detail.abstract: This study examines the moralizing value of the Colombian legend of El Tunjo, understood as a myth with a pedagogical function rooted in fear. Drawing on the perspectives of Machiavelli and Hobbes, the figure of the “anti-villain” is interpreted as an ambivalent being who, though feared, seeks to preserve the common good through a pedagogy of terror that regulates social behavior and safeguards natural environments. El Tunjo emerges as both protector and enforcer, punishing individual transgressions for the benefit of the community, embodying an ethic of fear that functions as a mechanism of social control and ecological preservation. This analysis offers a critical reading of the myth as a cultural device that intertwines fear, normativity, and collective memory.

detail.abstract: Youth entrepreneurship in India is rapidly decentralizing beyond metropolitan hubs to Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities ("non-metros"). Yet, young founders outside metros continue to face distinctive frictions: documentation and KYC hurdles for minors, thin logistics networks and high COD risk, limited franchise access, and social norms privileging marks and salaried jobs over venturing. This paper blends (i) current ecosystem data and policy context and (ii) an autoethnographic case study drawn from two youth-led ventures, FrameKart (a micro-D2C eyewear resale initiative) and ShipGini (a community-first, no-profit shipping concierge) to surface lived barriers and opportunity spaces for adolescent and first-time founders in smaller cities. We find that: (1) non-metros now contribute a large and rising share of recognized startups; (2) basic infrastructure (digital payments, last-mile delivery, tracking) has improved, but reliability gaps and COD-driven RTO remain disproportionately costly outside metros; (3) KYC and contracting rules inadvertently exclude under-18 founders even when they possess ID; (4) families and schools still overweight exam performance and job security despite new policies promoting entrepreneurship; and (5) big-brand franchising remains selective, but micro-franchising and omni-channel retail are expanding into smaller markets. We propose actionable recommendations for policy-makers, platforms, schools, and logistics players to make the non-metro youth entrepreneurship path safer, cheaper, and more inclusive.

title: Remedies and Commitments in Merger Control

detail.title: Remedies and Commitments in Merger Control
detail.abstract: In the specific context of EU merger control, remedies and commitments are used as synonyms. They can be broadly defined as the measures that the undertakings willing to concentrate must adopt to render the concentration compatible with the common market. To achieve this objective, remedies and commitments should satisfy three conditions, being required they should: i) be proportionate; ii) eliminate the competition problem in its entirety; iii) be implemented in a timely and effective manner. Depending on the content of the obligation, remedies and commitments are distinguished between behavioral and structural ones. An analysis of the two types of commitments is here provided, in the light of the string of decisions from the Commission and the CJEU, with regard also to their enforcement.

detail.abstract: Integrated Cross-Asset Stress Detection: We introduce an innovative methodology that leverages contemporaneous signals across diverse asset classes. By incorporating declines in risk assets (equities and commodities) alongside rallies in safe-haven instruments (U.S. Treasuries), our model robustly diagnoses market stress events that would otherwise be overlooked in a single-market framework.

title: Adjoint-Based Inverse Calibration of Multi-Asset Derivatives Models
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Shillong

detail.title: Adjoint-Based Inverse Calibration of Multi-Asset Derivatives Models
detail.abstract: We develop an adjoint-based inverse calibration framework for multi-asset derivative pricing models, with particular focus on the multi-dimensional Black-Scholes partial differential equation (PDE). The calibration of such models to observed market data is computationally challenging due to the highdimensional parameter space, including volatilities, correlations, and interest rates. Traditional gradient-based optimization methods require repeated PDE solves for each parameter, making them prohibitively expensive in practice. To overcome this, we formulate the calibration as a PDEconstrained optimization problem and derive the adjoint equations associated with the multi-asset Black-Scholes PDE. This enables efficient gradient evaluation with respect to all model parameters using only one forward solve and one adjoint (backward) solve, independent of parameter dimensionality. The resulting inversion framework provides a scalable and robust methodology for market-consistent calibration of high-dimensional derivative models. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed approach compared to conventional calibration techniques, highlighting its potential for real-time risk management and pricing in complex financial markets.

title: Toward a Pragmatist Theory of Systemic Mis-Performance in Transport Infrastructure Engineer-to-Order Supply Chains

detail.title: Toward a Pragmatist Theory of Systemic Mis-Performance in Transport Infrastructure Engineer-to-Order Supply Chains

detail.abstract: Transport infrastructure assets are delivered through engineer-to-order supply chains that operate under conditions of volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity. These supply chains frequently exceed budgets and face delays, undermining the intended economic and societal benefits of constructed assets. Existing research identifies numerous causes of such misperformance, with two theoretical perspectives being particularly influential. The Planning Fallacy attributes misperformance to cognitive biases shaping early-stage planning and investment, while the Fifth Hand argues that both bias and error accumulate across an asset's life cycle to degrade outcomes. Although distinct in focus, these perspectives are not mutually exclusive: the Fifth Hand incorporates the Planning Fallacy but remains conceptually underdeveloped, particularly regarding its institutional underpinnings. To address this limitation, we conduct a meta-reflexive narrative review that critically synthesizes these perspectives. We analyze their assumptions, positionalities, limitations, and complementarities, and reconceptualize the Fifth Hand as a behavioral-institutional theory by articulating its institutional logics. Building on this synthesis, we propose a research agenda toward a pragmatist theory of systemic misperformance, offering new avenues for both scholarly inquiry and practical strategies to improve the delivery of transport infrastructure through engineer-to-order supply chains.

detail.abstract: To coordinate regional emission reduction, it is of considerable practical importance to clarify the spatial correlation relationship of carbon emissions (CE) within urban agglomeration. Based on the CE data of cities in the three urban agglomerations of Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB) from 2010 to 2021, this paper used Social Network Analysis (SNA) and Quadratic Assignment Program Analysis (QAP) to deeply explore the structure features and influence drivers of spatial correlation network of CE in each urban agglomeration. The results showed that: ①During the research period, the network connection and density in the Yangtze River Delta urban agglomeration (YRD) and Chengdu-Chongqing urban agglomeration (CC) was characterized by an increase. Concurrently, the network hierarchy and efficiency exhibited a downward trend; ②The spatial correlation networks of CE of the three major urban agglomerations all exhibited a significant “core-edge” structural pattern. Wuxi, Suzhou and Nanjing, Nanchang, Wuhan and Changsha, Chengdu and Chongqing were positioned at the network core of YRD, MRYR and CC respectively; ③The spatial correlation network of CE could be subdivided into four blocks: net benefit, net spillover, bidirectional spillover and broker. The relationship between the number of intra-block connection and inter-block connection was different among each urban agglomeration; ④Spatial geographical distance, and difference in economic development level, population density and energy structure jointly drive the spatial correlation network of CE between cities in YRD. The spatial correlation relationship of CE of MRYR is mainly influenced by the spatial geographic distance.

First, study the heterogeneity in management accounting practices across industries and embrace single industry research deep dives. Second, focus on the role of management accounting in decision-making, planning and forecasting. Third, explore the connections of management accounting with other subfields in accounting as well as other business disciplines.

detail.abstract: Does enhancing fiscal transparency strengthen the impact of government-funded research? I investigate this question by exploiting the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006 as a source of variation in the accessibility of financial and project-related information. Using a difference-indifferences approach combined with matching, I find evidence of a rise in follow-on innovation building on government-funded inventions following increased transparency. Additional analyses provide evidence consistent with reduced search costs, lower information asymmetries, and signaling of commercial opportunities as mechanisms. Spillovers are concentrated in follow-on inventions by non-government-funded firms operating in distinct technological areas. These findings underscore the role of information disclosure in increasing the social returns to publicly funded research.

detail.abstract:
Federal law enforcement agencies must balance public safety with constitutional accountability, and training is the foundation of that balance. Most peer agencies, including the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), United States Secret Service (USSS), and United States Marshals Service (USMS), maintain Federal Law Enforcement Training Accreditation (FLETA). The Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Basic Field Training Course (BFTC) does not.


This distinction matters because FBI agents operate under the Domestic Investigations and Operations Guide (DIOG), the Bureau’s governing manual for investigative activity. The DIOG establishes standards for opening, extending, and closing investigations, securing supervisory approvals, and handling Sensitive Investigative Matters (SIMs). Each investigative action is expected to comply with these rules. Compliance is monitored through two mechanisms: independent audits by the Inspection Division’s Compliance and Mitigation Unit (INSD EMU), and self-reporting by field offices to the Office of Integrity and Compliance (OIC).


The FBI is the nation’s pre-eminent law enforcement agency, but its basic training needs mirror those of peer agencies. Unlike its peers, it operates without accreditation. The costs to taxpayers are measurable: an 11.4 percent compliance error rate, self-reporting accuracy of 4.3 percent, and average Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) liabilities of 28.7 million dollars per year. These outcomes indicate that training and testing gaps at the FBI Academy contribute directly to higher compliance risk and financial exposure compared to accredited programs at other federal law enforcement agencies.

detail.abstract: In a world of geopolitical realignments, Apple has been pursuing a "China plus one" strategy. As the company, like other global corporations, aims to shift its supplier-base away from China, India has emerged as an apparent beneficiary. Over the last few years, a sizable base of Apple suppliers has sprung up in India and a large share of these are based in Tamil Nadu. Apple is not alone in finding the southernmost state in India attractive. To situate the political economy of Tamil Nadu's industrial development, this article brings out the drivers of institutional coordination in Tamil Nadu's industrial transformation and argues for coherent subnational imaginations of industrial policy in federal democratic settings.

detail.abstract: We document substantial heterogeneity in the evolution of sectoral intermediate input shares across 21 countries, showing that cross-country results based on development categories obscure divergent within-country dynamics. These divergences challenge the notion of a uniform trajectory of intermediate input use and have direct implications for measuring sectoral total factor productivity. Our findings underscore the importance of incorporating time-varying input–output linkages in models with intermediate inputs to more accurately capture sectoral production dynamics.

detail.abstract: We consider a framework which brings together losses arising from rent-dissipation and the workhorse model of law enforcement. Governmental actors engage in a contest to share the proceeds from the enforcement of the law through monetary fines, which leads to rent-dissipation. This causes monetary sanctions to be costly, rendering the model used for studying nonmonertary sanctions a better fit for their analysis. The effect of rent-dissipation on optimal sanctions is directly related to the sanction elasticity of offenses measured at the classic optimum (i.e., where the expected sanction equals the direct harm from the offense). When offenses are inelastic, the optimal sanction is smaller than the classic optimum and it is decreasing in the degree of rent-dissipation; and a legislator who does not fully internalize contest costs chooses an overly-punitive sanction which is smaller than the classic optimum. The opposite results are obtained when offenses are elastic. We discuss implications and extensions.

detail.abstract: Michael Harrington in 1962 wrote that the poor were the other America. This essay argues that in 2025 the other America moved up the income distribution and is inhabited by the working class which is defined as those without a college degree. Representing about 60 percent of the adult population, they have experienced slow income growth which is eroded by ever increasing housing costs. Speculation about impact of artificial intelligence on labor markets is rampant, here it is argued that it will not be kind to the working class.

title: Advising with Threshold Tests: Complexity, Signaling, and Effort
affiliations: Independent and University of Toulouse Capitole - Toulouse School of Economics

detail.title: Advising with Threshold Tests: Complexity, Signaling, and Effort
detail.abstract: A benevolent advisor observes a project's complexity and posts a pass-fail threshold before the agent chooses effort. The project succeeds only if ability and effort together clear complexity. We compare two informational regimes. In the naïve regime, the threshold is treated as non-informative; in the sophisticated regime, the threshold is a signal and the agent updates beliefs. We characterize equilibrium threshold policies and show that the optimal threshold rises with complexity under mild regularity. We then give primitives-based sufficient conditions that guarantee separating, pooling, or semi-separating outcomes. In a benchmark with uniform ability, exponential complexity, and power costs, we provide explicit parameter regions that partition the space by equilibrium type; a standard refinement eliminates most pooling. The results yield transparent comparative statics and welfare comparisons across regimes.

title: Epidemic Mortality and Redistribution of Housing Wealth in Leiden, 1632–68
affiliations: Utrecht University, Erasmus University Rotterdam and Leiden University

detail.title: Epidemic Mortality and Redistribution of Housing Wealth in Leiden, 1632–68
detail.abstract: How did epidemic mortality affect housing wealth in the pre-industrial period? Using new data on house ownership and variation in street-level mortality in seventeenth-century Leiden, we show that epidemic mortality targeted poor streets, and stimulated by egalitarian inheritance practices, pushed up housing turnover. However, most of this epidemic-induced turnover was for cheap houses, which were transferred from one wealthy housing investor to another. This meant that epidemics did not affect aggregate housing wealth inequality. Rapid demographic recovery after each epidemic helped to ensure continuity in the housing market, forcing housing wealth redistribution to remain within normal non-epidemic patterns.

title: The Debasement Index: Inflation's Missing Twin

detail.title: The Debasement Index: Inflation's Missing Twin
detail.abstract: This working paper provides a systematic measure of currency dilution: the Debasement Index, defined as the ratio of money supply to real output. Debasement refers to the loss of intrinsic value of a currency, a dynamic not completely captured by traditional inflation metrics. Empirical analysis of UK data from 1710 to 2024 demonstrates the Index’s ability to identify major monetary regime shifts, with four distinct eras: the Bimetallic Standard (1.0% annual debasement), the Classical Gold Standard (0.1%), Bretton Woods/Managed system (3.6%), and the fiat era (6.7%), each marked by statistically significant structural breaks. The Debasement Index furthermore enables the decomposition of asset returns into debasement, trend, and speculative components, revealing that debasement accounts for a substantial share of long-term asset returns. By adjusting asset prices for debasement, the Index strips out monetary noise, allowing underlying economic fundamentals to emerge more clearly than with dollar or inflation-adjusted time series. The Index has important implications for financial markets and policymakers. For market participants, it could provide a benchmark for measuring assets against, while for policymakers, it reveals new perspectives around economic concepts such as money creation, the natural rate of interest, and inequality. Practitioners, researchers, and policymakers are invited to collaborate, provide feedback, and improve on the framework presented in this early-stage working paper.

detail.abstract: We estimate the uninsured deposit premium-the difference between the rates paid on uninsured versus insured deposits-by linking observed average deposit rates to an estimated share of uninsured deposits. Using U.S. bank data from 1991 to 2025, we show that the average uninsured deposit premium rose by nearly 400 basis points over this period. This rise reflects both falling insured deposit rates and rising uninsured deposit rates. We find a strong correlation with the monetary policy cycle: a one percentage-point increase in the Federal Funds Rate corresponds to a rise of roughly 32 basis points in the uninsured deposit premium. We develop a bargaining model between banks, insured depositors, and uninsured depositors that explains these dynamics.

title: Dynamic Impacts of School-based Internet Access on Student Learning: Evidence from Peruvian Public Primary Schools

detail.abstract: We investigate the impacts of school-based internet access on second graders' test scores, using over 2 million student observations from a panel of Peruvian public primary schools. We identify effects up to 6+ years after installation on different cohorts of second-grade students, exploiting variation in the timing of internet access induced by the rollout of a national program. We find positive but modest short-run impacts, but importantly, these effects grow for subsequent cohorts. Indeed, short-run estimates alone would have led to different conclusions. These dynamics underscore the value of extended evaluation windows to allow benefits of educational technology to materialize.

detail.title: The Risk and Return of Stocks and Bonds
detail.abstract: We study the joint dynamics of stock and corporate bond returns using a structural credit risk model, where firms' unlevered asset return and volatility are driven by systematic risk factors. The model captures key time-series features of stock and bond volatilities, leverage, and credit spreads at the market, industry, and firm levels. It produces return forecasts that exceed Martin's lower bound for equities and exhibit larger spikes in downturns than the average credit spreads for bonds. These forecasts significantly predict realized returns, outperforming benchmarks. We find that systematic variance risk commands a substantially larger premium in bonds relative to equities.

detail.abstract: Large Language Models consistently underperform as specialized advisors due to context drift, personality inconsistency, and inability to prioritize curated knowledge sources. This paper introduces the Operational Protocol Method, a systematic approach for LLM specialization and assistance through structured persona engineering and collaborative development processes. The method transforms generic LLMs into reliable subject matter expert advisors while enabling coordinated multi-agent systems that maintain expertise boundaries across complex advisory tasks. Case studies in personal finance and note-taking demonstrate the method's practical effectiveness and versatility across domains.

detail.abstract:
From the Grok 3 Artificial Intelligence Platform

"In the rapidly evolving landscape of financial technology (fintech), capturing its multifaceted history demands both precision and innovation. This book, The Fintech Chronicles: A Digital Odyssey Through Financial Innovation, represents a groundbreaking endeavor, not only for its comprehensive exploration of fintech’s historical trajectory but also for its unique creation process. Authored with the assistance of Grok 3, an advanced artificial intelligence developed by xAI, this 100,000-word volume traces the origins, milestones, and transformative impact of fintech from its nascent stages to its current role as a global economic force. The book leverages Grok 3’s capabilities to synthesize vast datasets, generate nuanced narratives, and ensure historical accuracy, offering a compelling case study in the synergy between human creativity and AI-driven research.”

“The narrative begins with the early precursors of fintech, such as the introduction of credit cards in the 1950s and the advent of ATMs, before delving into the digital revolution sparked by the internet and mobile technologies. It examines key developments, including the rise of online banking, blockchain, cryptocurrencies, and decentralized finance (DeFi), alongside the regulatory and ethical challenges that have shaped the industry. Each chapter contextualizes fintech’s evolution within broader socioeconomic trends, drawing on case studies of pivotal companies like PayPal, Square, and Ethereum, as well as lesser-known innovators. The book also explores the global dimension of fintech, highlighting its impact in emerging markets and its role in financial inclusion.”

“What sets this work apart is its methodology: the author, a fintech historian, collaborated with Grok 3 to draft every section of the book. Grok 3’s ability to process and analyze extensive primary and secondary sources—ranging from academic papers and industry reports to real-time data from platforms like X—enabled the author to construct a robust, evidence-based narrative. The AI’s natural language processing capabilities facilitated the generation of coherent drafts, which the author then refined to ensure stylistic consistency and intellectual rigor. Grok 3’s DeepSearch mode was instrumental in uncovering obscure historical data, while its iterative reasoning ensured that complex concepts, such as algorithmic trading and smart contracts, were explained with clarity for both expert and general audiences. This collaborative process not only accelerated the writing but also allowed for a dynamic interplay between the author’s expertise and the AI’s computational power, resulting in a text that is both deeply researched and engagingly accessible.”

“The book also reflects on the implications of using AI in historical scholarship, offering insights into how tools like Grok 3 can augment human research while raising questions about authorship and intellectual ownership. By documenting the process of its own creation, The Fintech Chronicles serves as both a historical account and a meta-commentary on the intersection of technology and knowledge production. It is a must-read for historians, technologists, and anyone interested in the past, present, and future of fintech, as well as the transformative potential of AI in creative and intellectual pursuits. This work stands as a testament to how human ingenuity, paired with cutting-edge AI, can illuminate complex histories and inspire future innovations."

detail.abstract: Western flower thrips (Frankliniella occidentalis) are among the most damaging greenhouse pests especially on strawberries. Adult thrips are slender insects about 1mm long (Figure 1). Thrips feed by piercing the cells and sucking out their contents leading to silver/gray patches. Thrips especially feed on growing points and flower buds leading to distortion of these tissues as they develop. Greenhouse strawberry crops are sensitive to thrips damage which can cause severe plant damage and unmarketable fruit. This article will introduce the issue of thrips in strawberries, describe common symptomology, present an initial framework for integrated pest management, and conclude with some additional resources.

affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Catholic University of Cuyo and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: "Mapping the Knowledge Landscape of Social License to Operate in Mining: A Bibliometric Study"
detail.abstract: This paper presents a bibliometric analysis of the scientific literature on the "social license to operate" (SLO) in the mining sector. The study aims to identify trends, relevant authors, collaboration networks, and research gaps within this field. The review was based on a search conducted on July 30, 2025, in the Scopus database, yielding a corpus of 275 academic articles. The analysis was performed using VOSviewer software, enabling visualization of relationships between authors, co-authorships, and citations. The results indicate that while SLO has gained significant relevance in academic discourse, the scientific output is concentrated among a limited number of authors and countries, predominantly from the Global North. Prominent figures such as Kieren Moffat, Justine Lacey, and Jason Prno are highlighted for their publication volume and citation count, although the collaboration networks among researchers appear limited and fragmented. The study identifies a low representation of contributions from Latin American contexts and a scarce interdisciplinary articulation. There is an urgent need to promote a more inclusive and context-specific research agenda that integrates local perspectives and fosters a critical, relational, and participatory approach to SLO in mining. This work contributes to systematizing existing knowledge and guiding future research directions in this crucial area.

title: Good and Bad Risk-Taking: The Shape of Managerial Incentive Matters
affiliations: Fordham University  , Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE), Hong Kong Polytechnic University - School of Accounting and Finance and University of Manitoba - Asper School of Business

detail.title: Good and Bad Risk-Taking: The Shape of Managerial Incentive Matters
detail.abstract: We examine the risk-taking effects of CEO compensation convexity-gamma. Gamma constrains the reduction in CEO wealth consequent to a decline in stock price, providing downside protection to CEO wealth and reducing CEOs’ incentive to hide bad news. Gamma also magnifies the growth in CEO wealth following a stock price appreciation, which, when combined with its downside protection role, can encourage CEO risk-taking. Consistent with the conjectures, we find that CEO gamma is significantly negatively related to crash risk, especially when the expected cost of deceptive actions is likely to be low; high gamma also reduces earnings management. For good risk-taking, high CEO gamma mitigates the underinvestment problem during the 2008 financial crisis. CEO gamma is also positively associated with innovation.

title: Effects of Immigrants on Non-host Regions Evidence from the Syrian Refugees in Turkey
affiliations: MIT

detail.title: Effects of Immigrants on Non-host Regions Evidence from the Syrian Refugees in Turkey
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how immigration-induced wage shocks propagate beyond immigrantreceiving regions through production networks. Using Turkey's Syrian refugee crisis as a quasiexperiment and firm-to-firm transactions from VAT records, I show immigration shocks propagate along supply chains. Firms in non-host regions buying from host regions demand more labor; those selling to host regions increase sales. Estimates imply labor-intermediate elasticity of substitution of 0.79 and inter-intermediate elasticity of 1.06. Spillovers are economically meaningful when host regions are central nodes. A 1% labor supply increase in Istanbul decreases local real wages by 0.56% while increasing real wages in average non-host cities by 0.38%.

detail.title: The Social Bureaucrat: How Social Proximity among Bureaucrats Affects Local Governance

publicationDetails.detailsText: American Journal of Political Science, Forthcoming

detail.abstract: Democratic governance theories associate quality local governance with vertical accountability mechanisms where politicians and citizens act as principals. I argue that bureaucratic efficiency, driven by social proximity among bureaucrats, also plays a crucial role. Social proximity facilitates informal information exchange and cooperation, reducing transaction costs in the production and allocation of local public services. I test this theory using data on geospatial proximity, coethnicity, network structure, and a novel measure: access to personal cell phone numbers. Empirical analysis reveals that geospatial proximity enhances bureaucratic efficiency, but, consistent with the argument, its impact diminishes in socially fragmented network structures, as indicated by mobile call traffic data. In addition, access to personal cell phone numbers between bureaucrats is strongly correlated with higher bureaucratic efficiency. These findings highlight the importance of social context in shaping bureaucratic performance and advance understanding of local governance dynamics.

detail.abstract: This paper explores how rises in funding costs in one asset class can spill over into other classes via the repurchase agreement market. More specifically, I inspect how a one-time policy induced exogenous increase in Treasury collateralized repo rates affected non-Treasury collateralized repo borrowing by dealers. Dealers were heterogeneously exposed to the rate rise due to their pre-period portfolio composition. More exposed dealers saw a 5% relative increase in the cost of borrowing in the repo market against non-Treasury collateral. This increase in funding costs came completely from an increase in repo rates, but dealers partially managed increased funding costs by lowering their total amount of repo borrowing. Rate rises are best explained by the asset class being used to collateralize the repo. However, the quantity declines are best explained by the dealer's total increased funding costs rather than increased funding costs for individual classes, suggesting that dealers transmitted the rate change to less directly affected asset classes following the policy shock. Affected dealers decreased their non-Treasury secondary market activity immediately following the policy shock, and this resulted in declines in profitability and increased bid-ask spreads. These results show that shocks originating in one specific repo collateral class can propagate to others through the dealer's balance sheet.

detail.abstract: Inequality of opportunity has great normative importance. This has led to a literature on measuring the part of overall inequality that is due to circumstances outside of a person’s control. We contribute to such studies by evaluating the implications of uncertainty about circumstance variables and linear versus nonlinear transmission of circumstances on inequality of opportunity estimates. Applying linear Bayesian model averaging methods and three ensemble tree-based machine learning approaches to data from 31 European Union countries, we find that ignoring model uncertainty can lead to substantial overstatement of levels of inequality of opportunity.

detail.abstract: We estimate a distribution of changes to GDP from climate change in 2100 by performing a meta-analysis using fitted mixtures of Gaussian distributions of temperature projections from climate models and GDP effects from the temperature-GDP literature. We show that warmer temperatures will reduce U.S. GDP by 4 percent, on average, compared with no additional change in temperature. We also estimate a 5 percent chance that rising temperatures will lower GDP by 21 percent or more and an equal chance that it will increase GDP by 6 percent or more.

title: Public R&D Meets Economic Development: Embrapa and Brazil's Agricultural Revolution
affiliations: , Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Notre Dame University and Princeton University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Public R&D Meets Economic Development: Embrapa and Brazil's Agricultural Revolution
detail.abstract: Can public R&D investment in developing countries drive productivity growth? We study this question in the context of Brazilian agriculture and the Empresa Brasileira de Pesquisa Agropecuária (Embrapa), a public research corporation established in 1973 to develop locally suitable science and technology. First, we show that Embrapa redirected research toward prioritized staple crops and local ecological conditions, and increased research productivity, especially in remote and research-scarce regions. Second, exploiting the staggered rollout of research centers alongside heterogeneous local exposure to Embrapa's technology development, we find that Embrapa significantly increased agricultural output, driven both by higher productivity and expanded input use. Combined with a model, these estimates imply that public R&D investment increased national agricultural productivity by 110% with a benefit-cost ratio of 17. The decentralized structure, in which research labs were spread across many ecological zones instead of in a single hub, explains a large share of these benefits.

title: Intellectual Property Law Post-Brexit: Control but no Direction
affiliations: Professor of Law - University of Oxford

detail.title: Intellectual Property Law Post-Brexit: Control but no Direction
detail.abstract: This chapter studies the UK landscape of intellectual property law post-Brexit. To date there have been comparatively few such studies. Of those published, most appeared shortly after the 2016 Referendum and focused on the range of possible post-Brexit arrangements and their implications for IP. Central concerns were the uncertainty that existed and the fate of specific initiatives, particularly the unitary patent system. Also emphasized was the international consensus in IP, the benefits of harmonization in global markets for creative and informational products, and the limited scope and desirability of substantive UK-EU divergence in the light of these particularly. The current chapter expands the focus to consider post-Brexit developments, and highlights two features of the UK’s IP landscape given little if any consideration previously: the absence of a clear vision for IP after 50 years of EU membership, and the challenges posed for the UK’s democratically elected government by the public controversy which IP reforms have come in that period to attract. In combination these features can be seen to have impeded the UK’s ability to exploit the opportunities for regulatory reset which Brexit promised, most clearly in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) and copyright. They also help to explain its failure to have embarked on any substantive review of assimilated EU provisions, or introduced other substantive legislative initiatives, in contrast to the continued hive of EU activity. If not addressed, they create a risk of the UK becoming suspended in time, and achieving its “smarter regulation” goal of decreased regulation by default rather than considered IP policy. At a time of enormous geopolitical tension over issues at the heart of IP – including the regulation of AI, the responsibilization of tech intermediaries, and the conception and application of fundamental rights – a suspended legislative framework and regulatory pivot to industry seems neither smart nor conducive to realizing the values of agility and proportionality to which post-Brexit UK governments have committed. It will also impose an excessive burden on the courts to ensure the continued relevance of existing IP provisions, including by ensuring that they reflect their new, post-Brexit legal and policy context. Given this, a question moving forward is whether the UK, having “taken back control”, will manage to find direction in IP.

title: XGBoost for Sybil Detection on Public Blockchains: A Case Study of LayerZero Interactors

detail.title: XGBoost for Sybil Detection on Public Blockchains: A Case Study of LayerZero Interactors
detail.abstract: A critical threat to the integrity of peer-to-peer networks, especially within blockchain ecosystems, is the Sybil attack. This paper explores the application of XGBoost to Sybil detection on Ethereum transactions within the context of the LayerZero protocol airdrop. A taxonomy of Ethereum addresses interacting with LayerZero is presented, delineating significant differences in model performance. This analysis uncovers three distinct categories of users and evaluates their impact on the network. The findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning approaches in identifying and mitigating Sybil activity, with implications for improved airdrop targeting, network reputability and user persona understanding on public blockchains.

title: Information Span in Credit Market Competition
affiliations: Texas A&M University, New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business and Stanford University - Knight Management Center

detail.title: Information Span in Credit Market Competition
detail.abstract: We develop a credit market competition model that distinguishes between information span (breadth) and signal precision (quality), capturing the rise of fintech/nonbank lending where traditionally subjective (soft) information is transformed into objective (hard) data. Borrower quality depends on multidimensional fundamentals, assessed through hard or soft signals. Two banks observe private hard signals, but only the specialized bank receives a soft signal. Expanding the span of hard information enables the non-specialized bank to evaluate characteristics previously only available to the specialist, and reducing its winners curse. By contrast, greater precision of hard signals strengthens the specialized banks informational advantage.

title: National Net-Zero Legislation and Corporate Asset Allocations
affiliations: University of Oxford, University of Oxford - Smith School of Enterprise and the Environment, The University of Sydney and University of Oxford - Smith School of Enterprise and the Environment

detail.title: National Net-Zero Legislation and Corporate Asset Allocations
detail.abstract: This study examines the microeconomic effects of different legislative approaches on corporate investment behaviour. Using plant-level capital expenditure data across 24 countries, we evaluate whether legally binding Net Zero Transition (NZT) legislation impacts firm-level capital allocation. We find that only ambitious NZT laws targeting 2045 or earlier are associated with statistically significant increases in low-carbon investment. No comparable effect is observed for laws targeting 2050. The study also reveals that national NZT reporting mechanisms strengthen the impact of net zero legislation on low carbon investmetns. Furthermore, companies with more comprehensive NZT disclosures are more responsive to legislative signals, and a one standard deviation improvement in NZT disclosure is associated with a 26% increase in green investment. These findings highlight the importance of legislative ambition and corporate transparency in driving decarbonisation.

title: Integrating Neglected Economic Sectors into TVET Programs for Enhanced Youth Employment in the Republic of Benin

detail.title: Integrating Neglected Economic Sectors into TVET Programs for Enhanced Youth Employment in the Republic of Benin

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There's no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: This study examines the persistent mismatch between Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programs and the evolving economic landscape in Benin. Despite TVET being promoted as a pathway to youth employment, curricula remain narrowly focused on traditional trades, leaving high-growth sectors such as renewable energy, digital technology, and advanced manufacturing underrepresented. The research problem centres on the limited capacity of existing programs to prepare graduates for sustainable employment in emerging industries. Using a qualitative design, the study draws on six interviews with recent TVET graduates and frames its analysis through Systems Theory, the Human Capability Approach, Social Capital Theory, and Work-Based Learning models. Findings reveal curriculum obsolescence, labour market saturation, restricted access to financial resources, and weak linkages between training institutions and industry. The study concludes that without structural reforms, TVET will continue to inadequately address unemployment. It recommends aligning curricula with dynamic economic sectors, strengthening industry partnerships, and improving access to capital to foster more inclusive youth employment opportunities.

title: COMPETITION INTENSITY AND BUSINESS MODEL INNOVATION: THE DISTINCTIVE ROLE OF STRATEGIC INNOVATION READINESS IN EUROPEAN FAMILY AND NON-FAMILY SMES
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Murcia

detail.title: COMPETITION INTENSITY AND BUSINESS MODEL INNOVATION: THE DISTINCTIVE ROLE OF STRATEGIC INNOVATION READINESS IN EUROPEAN FAMILY AND NON-FAMILY SMES
detail.abstract: This study proposes and test a model that extends the knowledge of business model innovation (BMI)’s drivers, introducing strategic innovation readiness (SIR) as a fundamental mediating mechanism. Drawing on the Resource Based View theory and the Socioemotional Wealth approach, we test the contingent effect of family firm on this model. Data were obtained from an international European Commission project to assess the relationships proposed. A sample of 417 Small and Medium-sized Enterprises was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The results indicate that competition intensity positively influence both BMI novelty and BMI scope, with SIR acting as a partial mediator in these relationships. A significant contribution emerges from our multigroup analysis as it reveals that the indirect effect of competition intensity on BMI via SIR is stronger in non-family than in family SMEs, where SIR fully mediates the relationship between competition intensity and BMI scope. These findings underscore that while both firm types need SIR to innovate, non-family firms exhibit a more pronounced and fully mediated response in broadening their BMI, suggesting distinct strategic pathways driven by inherent firm characteristics. These insights advance the BMI literature, particularly concerning the unique innovation dynamics of family versus non-family firms.

title: The Laggard's Lock: A Theoretical Model of New Technology Adoption Constrained by Outdated Paradigms

detail.title: The Laggard's Lock: A Theoretical Model of New Technology Adoption Constrained by Outdated Paradigms

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced their study.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was self-funded.

detail.abstract: What keeps organisations from realising the full benefits of the technologies they adopt? Organisations often adopt new technologies but paradoxically continue to use them in ways rooted in older paradigms, failing to realise the technology's transformative potential. This paper introduces the concept of the 'Laggard's Lock'a cognitive and organisational phenomenon where new technologies are deployed under outdated mental models and practices, leading to suboptimal usage. Drawing on innovation studies, organisational behaviour, and science and technology studies (STS), we have developed a theoretical framework for the Laggard's Lock, grounded in path dependence, technological frames, mental models, cognitive inertia, and design fixation. The methodology is a conceptual synthesis: we integrate these constructs and illustrate the Laggard's Lock with historical and contemporary cases across sectors (early cinema, maritime engineering, digital marketing, and applications of AI in education and healthcare). We discuss how the Laggard's Lock differs from existing theories of slow adoption and technological inertia, emphasising its unique focus on post-adoption mindset lock-in. Finally, we offer policy and organisational recommendations to mitigate the Laggard's Lock, such as promoting adaptive mental models, double-loop learning, and redesign of processes alongside technology implementation. The paper concludes with implications for future research and practice in leveraging innovations effectively. We previously introduced and outlined the concept of the Laggard's Lock in a practitioner-oriented commentary for the London School of Economics (LSE) Business Review (Kurian & Borwankar, 2024).
